summary: Client calls createRazorpayOrder unconditionally after subscription/order creation; server 409s a zero-payable order, and the client has no branch to detect or recover from that case.
evidence: artifacts/storefront/lib/moneyPath.ts:142 finishPlanPayment, :240 finishAlacartePayment — createRazorpayOrder called unconditionally
artifacts/api-server/src/routes/payments.ts:272-275 — 409 'order has no payable amount' when authoritativePaise <= 0
artifacts/api-server/src/routes/subscriptions.ts:508-517 — settled: chargePaise === 0 computed server-side, never returned to or read by the client
impact: A customer whose first subscription cycle is fully covered by credit gets a generic 'Something went wrong' error instead of a confirmation, even though the subscription was created successfully.
reuseDecision: REUSE_WITH_ADAPTER — add a chargePaise/settled field to CreateSubscriptionResponse (and the à-la-carte order-create response) and branch in moneyPath.ts before calling createRazorpayOrder.

summary: /care/[condition] renders synthesized therapeutic copy for any arbitrary slug — no allowlist gate, no notFound(), conflicting with a prior documented product ruling that explicitly forbids adding one.
evidence: artifacts/storefront/app/(global)/care/[condition]/page.tsx — uses conditionDisplayName() only, no CARE_CONDITIONS check, no notFound()
artifacts/storefront/lib/conditionDisplay.ts — pure casing function, not a gate
artifacts/storefront/lib/careConditions.ts — allowlist exists but is wired only into /care's ConditionRail, not the detail route; its own comment records the conflicting ruling
impact: /care/asdfqwerty renders 'Asdfqwerty Protocol' with the same clinical-objectives boilerplate as an approved condition.
reuseDecision: BLOCKED_BY_PRODUCT_DECISION — this sweep's §13 and the prior TNM-CRO ruling conflict; needs clinical/product ownership to resolve, not a unilateral fix.
resolution: Decision (2026-08-11): keep the free-text catch-all (no notFound(), no new fetch surface, respecting the prior ruling), but strip the clinical framing for unmapped slugs. isCareConditionKnown() (lib/careConditions.ts) now gates COPY only, not the route — a known condition still renders 'Clinical Objectives' / RD-protocol language; an unmapped slug gets a plain, non-clinical page instead. Implemented in app/(global)/care/[condition]/page.tsx; regression coverage added in e2e/specs/condition-assessment-entry.spec.ts and lib/careConditions.test.ts.

summary: The approved ruling declares /corporate canonical and /corporate-wellness an alias to redirect, but /corporate is a live placeholder and /corporate-wellness is the real 138-line implementation — inverted from what §25 requires.
evidence: artifacts/storefront/app/(b2b)/corporate/page.tsx — PlaceholderPage, 'Clean slate placeholder pending implementation'
artifacts/storefront/app/(b2b)/corporate-wellness/page.tsx — 138 lines, substantive
artifacts/storefront/lib/nav.ts — COMPANY_LINKS links /corporate; Community group links both /corporate-wellness and /corporate side by side
impact: Production nav sends some clicks (COMPANY_LINKS 'Corporate') to a dead placeholder.
reuseDecision: Do not install the redirect as currently specified. Either migrate /corporate-wellness's content onto /corporate first, then redirect the alias — or formally flip which side is canonical.
resolution: Decision (2026-08-11): flip canonical status onto the real page. Removed the app/(b2b)/corporate/page.tsx placeholder; added a permanent (308) redirect /corporate -> /corporate-wellness in next.config.ts's shared redirects() map (same mechanism as the existing /quiz and /auth aliases). Updated every internal link that pointed at /corporate (lib/nav.ts COMPANY_LINKS + Community group, app/(b2b)/layout.tsx, app/(global)/plans/page.tsx, components/corporate/CompanyInvite.tsx) to target /corporate-wellness directly, and removed the now-duplicate 'Corporate & partnerships' nav entry. Removed /corporate from app/sitemap.ts (only the canonical destination belongs there). Regression coverage added in e2e/specs/compat-aliases.spec.ts.

summary: TrialStart's only purchase CTA is suppressed once cart.lines.length > 0, and FocusLayout (which hosts /trial) never mounts MiniCartBar to replace it — a customer with an existing cart sees no way to start the trial.
evidence: artifacts/storefront/components/trial/TrialStart.tsx:120 — {cart.lines.length === 0 && (...)}
artifacts/storefront/app/(focus)/layout.tsx — 'no Header, no MobileBottomNav, no Footer, no MiniCartBar' (verbatim)
reuseDecision: REUSE_WITH_REFACTOR — TrialStart needs its own always-visible sticky bar regardless of cart state (the FocusLayout convention every other focus-route CTA already follows), not a MiniCartBar handoff that doesn't exist in this shell.
resolution: Fixed (2026-08-11): removed the cart.lines.length === 0 guard — the sticky Start bar in components/trial/TrialStart.tsx now always renders, since FocusLayout mounts no MiniCartBar to ever hand the bottom edge to (cart state or not, nothing else can occupy it). Regression coverage added in e2e/specs/cuj-04-trial.spec.ts ('the start CTA stays visible and clickable even with items already in cart').

summary: PantryVisionScanner's 'Add to Subscription' button has no onClick handler — a bare <button> with zero behavior.
evidence: artifacts/storefront/components/wellness/PantryVisionScanner.tsx:104-107
impact: Terminal CTA on a real, wired AI feature does nothing when pressed.
reuseDecision: REUSE_WITH_REFACTOR — wire to the existing addons/cart mutation path; also flagged for a design-token pass (raw Tailwind palette classes, not the token system the rest of the storefront uses).
resolution: Fixed (2026-08-11): the server's suggestedTanmatraAddOns (lib/pantryVisionScanner.ts) are catalogue dishes sliced off the menu, not a subscription add-on (AddOnId is a fixed 2-value enum with an incompatible shape) — so the cart mutation path was the correct one, not the addons API. Wired the button to lib/cartStore.ts's addLine via useCart(), the same mechanism CustomBuildHub already uses, and relabeled it 'Add to cart' (was 'Add to Subscription', which no longer matched the actual mutation). Regression coverage added in e2e/specs/stitch-runtime/account.spec.ts ('pantry scan suggestion Add to cart adds a real cart line'). The raw-Tailwind design-token cleanup flagged in reuseDecision is intentionally NOT part of this fix — out of scope for a CTA-wiring defect; still open as a follow-up.

summary: LandingHero.tsx renders its hero section as a semantic <header>, so any page that composes it inside a shell that already has its own chrome <header> (app/(b2b)/layout.tsx) ends up with two <header> elements in the DOM.
evidence: artifacts/storefront/components/landing/LandingHero.tsx:33 — <header className="border-b border-line py-[var(--space-section)]">

Surfaced by e2e/specs/single-chrome.spec.ts's b2b-shell test once it was pointed at the real /corporate-wellness page instead of the old placeholder — the placeholder never had a second header to catch this.
3 active pages compose LandingHero: /corporate-wellness, /partners/gyms, /partners/fitness-clubs — same issue likely on all three, only /corporate-wellness was directly re-verified this pass.
impact: Two <header> landmarks on one page is an accessibility anti-pattern (ambiguous 'banner' landmark for screen-reader users) — not a functional break. The e2e test was scoped to the shell header specifically (filtered by the 'Business' nav it wraps) rather than asserting a bare header count, so this doesn't block the /corporate redirect work; recorded as a separate, pre-existing, unfixed finding.
reuseDecision: REUSE_WITH_REFACTOR — change LandingHero's hero wrapper from <header> to <section>; it is page-body content, not a document/page-level introductory landmark.
